text: I watched workers finish a careful trench at Tel Maridun on Tuesday morning as Dr. Yara Lindqvist, the dig’s lead archaeologist, stood beside the north wall with her clipboard and radio. Lindqvist told the Gazette she had directed the excavation since its opening in early April, after a survey team flagged the site for unusual stone alignments. By noon, her crew had exposed two lamp fragments, a bronze pin, and what she called “a remarkably intact storage floor” beneath a collapsed room. Site foreman Elias Venn said the team of 18 had logged every layer before noon heat halted the dig. Lindqvist said the season would continue through 14 July, weather permitting.
